summary.en: A single vowel mark at the end of a word can change a sentence's whole meaning. This lesson explains what Arabic grammar (nahw) is, what it is for, how it began, and its best-known schools, scholars and books.

title.en: What Is Speech (Kalam) to the Grammarians, and What Are Its Three Parts?

summary.en: What counts as speech (kalam) for the Arabic grammarians, and what makes a sentence meaningful? This lesson covers the definition of kalam and its four conditions, then its three parts — noun, verb and particle — with a worked example from Ibn Qutayba.

description.en: What counts as speech (kalam) for the Arabic grammarians, and what makes a sentence meaningful? This lesson covers the definition of kalam and its four conditions (uttered, compound, meaningful, by convention), then its three parts: the noun and its types, the verb and its categories, and the particle — letters of construction versus letters of meaning — with an applied reading of a passage by Ibn Qutayba from the introduction to Adab al-Katib.

description.en: How do you know a word is a noun? Is the ta in «حضرتُ» a noun? This lesson covers the five signs of the noun that Ibn Malik gathered in a single line of verse: the genitive (jarr), tanwin, the vocative, the definite article «أل», and predication (isnad) — any one of them is enough to identify a noun.

summary.en: A single verb such as «كَتَبَ» carries six descriptions at once. This lesson covers the categories of the verb: tense, inflection, sound and weak roots, bare and augmented forms, transitivity, voice, and frozen versus conjugable verbs.

description.en: «ليسَ العلمُ بضارٍّ»: is «ضارٍّ» simply a genitive noun and nothing more? This lesson covers the Arabic prepositions (huruf al-jarr), Ibn Malik's two lines of verse that gather all twenty of them, the meanings of the most common ones, how a preposition carries the verb's meaning to the noun, their three types — original, redundant and quasi-redundant — and the i'rab of a noun governed by a redundant preposition.

description.en: «رأيتُ الطالباتَ» or «رأيتُ الطالباتِ»? Many pick the fatha because the word is an object, but the correct ending is the kasra. This lesson classifies the Arabic noun from four angles: gender (masculine and feminine), number (singular, dual and plural, and how each is inflected), definiteness and the seven kinds of definite nouns, and primitive versus derived nouns.

description.en: «حضرَ محمدٌ، رأيتُ محمدًا، حظيتُ بمحمدٍ»: one word, so why does its ending change three times, while «كيفَ» never changes? This lesson covers the meaning of i'rab, how the governing word ('amil) changes the case of nouns and present-tense verbs, overt vs. implied (taqdiri) case marks and the three things that hide them, and bina' (fixed endings) with its four forms.

summary.en: Why does the ending of «محمد» change while «كيفَ» never does? Learn what i'rab is and how the governing word drives it, overt vs. implied case marks and their three causes, and bina' with its four forms.

description.en: «يَسُرُّني أنْ تنجحَ»: the verb «يَسُرُّ» needs a subject, so where is it? This lesson covers the explicit verbal noun (masdar sarih) and its heard vs. regular patterns, the interpreted verbal noun (masdar mu'awwal) and its six masdar particles, how to turn it back into an explicit masdar, and how to parse it by its position in the sentence.

summary.en: In «يَسُرُّني أنْ تنجحَ», where is the subject of «يَسُرُّ»? Learn the explicit verbal noun and its patterns, the interpreted verbal noun and its six particles, and how to convert and parse it by position.

description.ar:
أَكَلَ وقَالَ: كلاهما يبدو فيه ألِف، لكنّ أحدَهما صحيحٌ والآخرَ معتلّ. فأيُّهما المعتلّ؟ ولماذا؟
في هذا الدرس نعرف الفرق بين الفعل الصحيح والفعل المعتل، وأنواعَ كلٍّ منهما: السالم والمهموز والمضعّف، والمثال والأجوف والناقص، وكيف نحكم على الفعل المضارع بالرجوع إلى ماضيه.

description.en: Akala and qala both seem to contain an alif, yet one is a sound verb and the other a weak one. This lesson explains sound verbs (salim, mahmuz, muda'af) and weak verbs (mithal, ajwaf, naqis), and how to classify a present-tense verb by going back to its past form.

summary.ar: أَكَلَ وقَالَ: أيُّهما الفعل المعتل؟ درسٌ يشرح الفعل الصحيح بأنواعه (السالم والمهموز والمضعّف) والفعل المعتل بأنواعه (المثال والأجوف والناقص)، وكيف تحكم على المضارع بالرجوع إلى ماضيه.
